profileName: PolLead — Tech Team Leadership, Clarity & 1:1 Feedback (C1)

watchOuts.title: Lead With the Decision or Takeaway Before Unpacking Technical Context
watchOuts.detail: Senior engineers naturally explain architecture chronologically before stating the conclusion. In team meetings and stakeholder presentations, flip the order: state the headline decision in sentence one ('We are deferring the migration to Q3 to protect checkout stability'), then give two crisp supporting reasons.

watchOuts.tag: Polish-to-C1 Polish · Directness vs. UK Diplomatic Hedging
watchOuts.title: Softening Constructive 1:1 Feedback Without Losing Clarity
watchOuts.detail: Polish workplace communication prizes directness, whereas UK tech teams expect warm framing around tough feedback. Pair explicit standards with collaborative curiosity: instead of 'Your PRs are too slow and unclear', use 'I'd like to tighten our PR turnaround—what's currently blocking smaller, clearer diffs?'

watchOuts.title: Zero-Article Generalizations vs. Specific Deliverables
watchOuts.detail: Even at C1, fast-paced meeting speech can drop articles before singular deliverables ('We need clear rollout plan' → 'We need a clear rollout plan') or pluralize uncountables ('feedbacks', 'equipments', 'softwares'). Keep 'feedback', 'code', and 'progress' strictly singular.

watchOuts.title: Final Consonant Voicing & British/Neutral Stress Rhythm
watchOuts.detail: Keep final consonants voiced in high-frequency leadership words ('lead' vs. 'leet', 'build' vs. 'built', 'merge' vs. 'merch') and let unstressed syllables reduce cleanly so key verbs and metrics punch through in hybrid calls.

watchOuts.title: Cutting 'Let Me Just Quickly Explain...' Openers
watchOuts.detail: Eliminate throat-clearing disclaimers before speaking in leadership forums. Replace 'Sorry, just to quickly jump in and add one small thing...' with 'One critical risk to flag here is...'

scenarios.title: Running a Crisp 10-Minute Architecture Decision Meeting
scenarios.prompt: Your squad is split between two technical approaches and spinning in circles. Step in as team lead, summarize the trade-off in two sentences, state the decision clearly, and align everyone on next steps without over-explaining.

scenarios.title: Delivering Tough 1:1 Feedback to a Talented but Distracted Senior Dev
scenarios.prompt: A strong engineer on your team has been missing code-review SLAs and dominating sprint planning. Give direct, unambiguous feedback that sets clear expectations while keeping the tone grounded, respectful, and collaborative.

scenarios.title: Presenting a Slipping Roadmap to Non-Technical Leadership
scenarios.prompt: You need to tell product and commercial leads outside London that a release is shifting by two weeks. Present the revised timeline with calm authority—leading with business impact, trade-offs, and mitigation rather than defensive technical jargon.

scenarios.title: Unplugging: Why Cold Plunges & Wood-Fired Saunas Sharpen Engineering Judgment
scenarios.prompt: Pitch the real cognitive recovery benefits of serious sauna rounds and cold-water immersion to a burned-out engineering peer who never steps away from their screen. Keep your pacing unhurried and vivid.

scenarios.title: Navigating a Rainy Ridge Walk in the Peaks or Chilterns When Plans Change
scenarios.prompt: Tell a concise story about an outdoor trail or weather detour outside London where calm assessment beat stubbornness—and draw a subtle parallel to leading a team through production uncertainty.

customCards.term: Executive Clarity Upgrade: "Because of database latency and legacy coupling, we need to delay the launch."
customCards.definition: "We're pushing the launch by two weeks to protect system reliability—here are the two bottlenecks we're resolving first."
customCards.example: Lead with the headline decision so stakeholders know why the technical details matter.
customCards.note: BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front): State the decision first, then unpack supporting evidence.

customCards.term: 1:1 Feedback Calibration: "Your pull requests are too big and take too long for the team to review."
customCards.definition: "I want to make code reviews faster and easier for the whole squad—let's break upcoming PRs into smaller, self-contained chunks."
customCards.example: What would help us get your changes reviewed within 24 hours this sprint?
customCards.note: UK Tech Register: Pairs direct standards with shared problem-solving rather than blunt critique.

customCards.term: Meeting Authority Upgrade: "Sorry to interrupt, I just wanted to quickly mention one small concern about deployment."
customCards.definition: "Before we lock this in, I want to flag one deployment risk we need to account for."
customCards.example: Cutting apologetic fillers immediately signals calm team-lead ownership.
customCards.note: Presence & Conciseness: Drop 'just', 'quickly', and 'small' when raising substantive engineering points.

customCards.term: Grammar & Countability Check: "We got useful feedbacks from the team and made a good progress on the release."
customCards.definition: "We got useful feedback from the team and made good progress on the release."
customCards.example: Both 'feedback' and 'progress' are uncountable—never add '-s' or 'a' before them.
customCards.note: Polish-to-C1 Polish: Eliminate plural '-s' and indefinite articles on uncountable nouns.

customCards.term: 1:1 Coaching Question: How do you invite ownership from a quiet mid-level developer without putting them on the spot?
customCards.definition: "You've been closest to this service all week—how would you weigh the trade-off if it were your call?"
customCards.example: Inviting their judgment builds autonomy far faster than assigning instructions.
customCards.note: Leadership Leverage: Open-ended ownership questions elevate team-wide thinking.

customCards.term: Presentation Transition: "Now I finished talking about the problem, so next I will show the solution."
customCards.definition: "That's the bottleneck in plain terms—now let's look at how we eliminate it in Q3."
customCards.example: Clean signposting keeps executive audiences anchored during technical walkthroughs.
customCards.note: Signposting: Replace mechanical narration with crisp, forward-looking transitions.

customCards.term: Pronunciation Drill (Final Voicing): "The lead dev merged a solid build and logged every edge case."
customCards.definition: Hold a brief vocal-cord buzz on each final consonant: lead · dev · merged · solid · build · logged · edge.
customCards.note: Polish L1 Polish: Preventing final-consonant devoicing sharpens intelligibility on headset mics.
